links.outcome: Sex-based accuracy parity difference of baseline COVID-19 severity model
links.effect: Baseline model achieved 90.68% accuracy but exhibited a 10.11% Subset Accuracy Parity Difference between sexes, indicating a relatively large bias.
links.quote: The baseline (unmitigated) classification model achieved 90.68% accuracy but exhibited a 10.11% Subset Accuracy Parity Difference between sexes, indicating a relatively large bias.

links.outcome: Fairness (SAPD, LEOD) and accuracy after bias mitigation methods versus baseline
links.effect: XAI-based mitigation reduced sex-based disparities without significant accuracy loss, with a better fairness-accuracy trade-off than three traditional mitigation methods that compromised accuracy more.
links.quote: The XAI-driven bias mitigation intervention effectively reduces sex-based disparities in COVID-19 severity prediction without the significant accuracy loss observed in traditional methods.

unlisted_practices: SHAP-based identification of sex-sensitive feature interactions for model retraining

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating and comparing algorithmic bias mitigation strategies (including an XAI-based mitigation technique) to reduce sex-based disparities in a clinical COVID-19 severity risk model.
